title: The four-colour theorem and Bring's surface
html: The classical four-colour theorem dictates that every planar graph is four-colourable. For higher-genus surfaces, the chromatic number grows as O(\sqrt{g}) (Heawood conjecture, proved by Ringel--Youngs). That Bring's surface attains the planar bound of four at genus 4 reflects the rigidity imposed by its S_5 symmetry. In the Descartes universe, the trivial bundle \mathcal{S}=\mathcal{S}_0 (radial projection) carries no torsion. The resulting flatness of the tessellation forces the same chromatic economy as the sphere.
